title: Plasma can be DDOSed by applications sending too many notifications in short intervals
line: An app that floods Plasma with notifications no longer freezes the shell: each app can show at most 50 new notifications every 10 seconds.
explanation: The notification server accepted every Notify call. Each one went through app identification (including a synchronous D-Bus PID lookup), the notifications model and popup handling, so 10000 notifications kept plasmashell's main thread at 100% CPU for about 11 s, grew it by about 850 MB, and queued every other D-Bus call and click behind them. Now Notify counts new (not replacing) notifications per application, keyed by desktop-entry hint, else app name, else sender. Above 50 in a 10-second window it refuses them right away with the existing ExcessNotificationGeneration error, before doing any other work.

commits.message:
libnotificationmanager: rate limit new notifications per application

An application sending thousands of notifications in a burst kept the
shell busy for many seconds and grew its memory by about a gigabyte. Now
each application may create at most 50 notifications every 10 seconds.

BUG: 483481

media.caption: Master, 2 s after clicking the launcher during a 10000-notification burst: the launcher hasn't opened and a stray popup is drawn at the top of the screen
With the fix, same burst and click: the launcher opens at once; only the first 50 notifications are shown
Master: the whole run. The shell is unresponsive for about 11 s and popups keep cycling through thousands of notifications
With the fix: same run. The excess is refused immediately and the shell stays responsive
